correctness.rationale: The quotient by xy,x^(a+1),y^(b+1) first gives two separate pure-monomial tails, and the remaining relation identifies exactly their terminal lines; this proves the basis and dimension. The two relations have height two and the joint annihilator of x,y is exactly the identified socle. For t≥2 mixed products vanish, including every product with the socle summand. In a surviving x-branch, the leading monomial u^t x^(ti) is nonzero regardless of characteristic. Positive powers of x applied to the generator give the entire strictly higher x-tail by triangular elimination, including the socle, and likewise for y. With two surviving subterminal leading monomials, the two tails share exactly the socle and the generator adds one line modulo both tails. A sole surviving subterminal branch gives that entire branch from the leading degree to the socle. If neither branch survives subterminally, only the stated scalar γ_t contributes, with c contributing at t=1 only. Thus with two nonzero branches the only coefficient-sensitive exponent is ti=a and tj=b. The profile at (∞,∞) must be read as the two separately counted zero/nonzero socle-only cases, as the rank formula and census specify. Differences of ranks give the block exponents; each prescribed pair of leading coefficients has q^(a+b−1−i−j) lifts. The cyclic-group power map makes the number of cancelling pairs (q−1)ρ_q(k), with the stipulated characteristic-two behavior. In the balanced example r_1=2n−2 forces both branches linear for n≥3, since any sole branch has rank at most n. Subsequent ranks are 2n−2t until t=n, where the 0/1 split gives exactly the two partitions. The independent 6×6 modular rank enumeration over F_3 of all 243 elements verified the six histogram counts 54,108,54,24,2,1 for (4,2),(4,1,1),(3,3),(2,2,1,1),(2,1^4),(1^6), respectively.
residual_risks: Finite reproduction is one check, not a proof across all fields. The general argument is exact and concerns the nilpotent regular-module action of the radical only.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the parameter-uniform all-radical-element finite-field multiplicity polynomial in the two-branch socle-glued complete intersections, especially the branch-valuation pairs and arithmetic terminal cancellation resolving the full census. The connected-sum construction, generic Jordan theory and cyclic-group count are not new. The strongest comparable finite-field censuses have different multiplication relations that change the surviving powers and the arithmetic of the split. The closest primary connected-sum and height-two Jordan treatments inspected do not give or imply this all-element census. The frozen reference to Example 5.17 in arXiv:1904.06297 is not a valid locator in the inspected version: 5.17 is a lemma, and the relevant field-dependence discussion at Remark 4.13 and Example 5.28 is different from the claimed census. This bibliographic issue does not change the mathematical finding.
residual_risks: Limited web results are not an absence proof; a general all-element stratum theorem specialized to this algebra remains a possible uninspected overlap.
The explicit preprint numbering discrepancy is noted without speculating about other editions.

value.rationale: This is a full census for a natural socle identification of two truncated one-variable algebras. It reports the frequency of every Jordan partition, including empty strata, without scanning a vector space of size q^(a+b−1). The arithmetic distinction is structural: exactly one rank can change, and an explicit power-map condition governs the existence and multiplicity of balanced top types even in small characteristic. Those are precise data for comparing finite-field Jordan strata beyond generic Lefschetz behavior.
residual_risks: No generalization is asserted for more branches, other modules, or scheme-theoretic multiplicities.
